--- title: link --- ```python link(df, scale, on, key='auto', errors='raise', ref=None) ``` Attach ``geo_id`` to a table that identifies units by name or by a source code. ## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} | Name | Type | Description | Default | |--------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------| | df | pd.DataFrame | Your table (one row per unit, or per unit and year) | _required_ | | scale | str | Scale of your units, e.g. ``"province"`` (see ``geo.scales()``) | _required_ | | on | str | The column of ``df`` that identifies the unit | _required_ | | key | str | The column of ``geo.units(scale)`` to match against: ``"name"``, a source code column of ``geo.units(scale)`` (e.g. ``"gid"`` for GADM codes), or ``"auto"``: the column matching most values, with the others filling the gaps (so mixed spellings from different sources still link). Matching ignores accents, case, spaces and punctuation ("BântéayMéanchey" = "Banteay Meanchey"). A value shared by several units (two municipalities with the same name) is ambiguous and links to none of them: link such units by a code instead. | `'auto'` | | errors | str | ``"raise"`` (default), ``"warn"`` or ``"ignore"`` for values that match no unit or are ambiguous | `'raise'` | ## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns} | Name | Type | Description | |--------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------| | | pandas.DataFrame | A copy of ``df`` with ``geo_id`` as its first column. | ## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example} ```python !pip install -q geo4bolivia import geo4bolivia as geo import plotly.express as px import pandas as pd mine = pd.DataFrame({"municipio": ["SUCRE", "el alto", "Cobija"], "clinics": [41, 63, 12]}) # made-up values mine = geo.link(mine, scale="map343", on="municipio") by_code = geo.link(pd.DataFrame({"cod": [20101]}), scale="map343", on="cod", key="mun_id") # INE code -> geo_id geo.add_names(mine) ``` ::: {#fd1e996f .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
geo_id name municipio clinics
0 BO-01-06-02 Sucre SUCRE 41
1 BO-04-17-02 El Alto el alto 63
2 BO-06-05-03 Cobija Cobija 12
``` ::: :::
